title: Fix the Unchecked Malloc Result
description: The program should allocate memory for an integer and store a value in it.
expectedBehavior: The program should safely allocate memory, store 42 in it, and print 42 — even in the rare case where memory allocation fails.
actualProblem: malloc() can return NULL if memory allocation fails, and this code never checks for that before dereferencing ptr. If malloc did fail, *ptr = 42 would dereference a NULL pointer, causing a crash.
explanation: malloc() signals failure by returning NULL rather than throwing an exception. Production-quality C code always checks the returned pointer before dereferencing it, to avoid crashing on a NULL pointer dereference.
